MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, APRIL 3, 2023

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by CHAIR YOO at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Yoo, Medawar, Olson, Romanelli, Nicklas, Schachter

  Commissioners Absent:  Friedman

  City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Dean Flores, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, MARCH 6, 2023

There being no objection, the Commission approved Item 4A.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER OLSON to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6A.

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

Items taken out of order.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220386; LOCATION: 39 Empty Saddle Road;
  APPLICANT: Michael Hasegawa (on behalf of Verizon Wireless); A request for a
  Conditional Use Permit (CUP-220387) for a new stealth telecommunication facility
  featuring a 64’-high monoeucalyptus structure located toward the rear of the property
  including 17 antennas (8 panel antennas, 4 CBRS antennas, 4 C-Band antennas, and 1
  microwave antenna) and 16 wireless radios on 4 arrays, a 342 square-foot lease area that
  features 3 equipment cabinets, 1 generator and will be fully enclosed with an 8’-high CMU
  wall.

Associate Planner Flores stated that the applicant has made several continuance requests for
this item. Staff recommends that this item be continued to a date uncertain. This item will be
noticed to a 500’ radius and the notice will be published in the paper 10 days prior to the scheduled
meeting.

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER OLSON to,

  CONTINUE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220386 TO A DATE UNCERTAIN.

AYES: Yoo, Medawar, Olson, Romanelli, Nicklas, Schachter
NOES:
ABSENT: Friedman
ABSTAIN:

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, APRIL 3, 2023
  1
 B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 230113; LOCATION: 4040 Palos Verdes Drive North,
  #101; APPLICANT: Yoo Jin Kang; A request for a Conditional Use Permit (CUP-230114)
  for a medical office use (acupuncture office) located in an existing office park.

Associate Planner Flores provided a presentation summarizing the staff report. The request is for
a CUP for an acupuncture office; it is by appointment, and there is one employee. The hours of
operation are Monday through Saturday from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The parking for the office
park is legal non-conforming, likely due to the parking standards being less stringent at the time
it was built and would not conform to the new parking standard, which was established in 1999.
Due to the low scale operation and appointment-based clientele, staff determined that there
should not be any adverse impact to the parking on the site.

Staff recommends that the Planning Commission, open the public hearing; take public testimony;
discuss the issues; close the public hearing; and adopt Resolution No. PA-230113, approving the
project, and in accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act (Public Resources Code
§ 21000 et seq.: “CEQA”), determine that the project is categorically exempt under Class 3,
Section 15303(a) - New Construction or Conversion of Small Structures.

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR inquired about other medical uses at this location. Associate Planner
Flores stated that, as far as staff is aware, this is the only one.

Laurie Inadomi Halvorsen, Resident and Leasing Agent, stated that there are other medical uses
and there was previously a dental office in the building.

Director Naughton stated that there are times that uses may go into buildings that staff is not
aware of; a dental office would have required a CUP had staff known that it was going into the
building.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER OLSON, Associate Planner Flores stated that this
application would only apply for Suite 101. However, the property owner may apply for a Master
CUP for the building, which would avoid the need for all the suites to go through the CUP process.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if there is a limit on the number of employees per square
foot. Director Naughton stated that the code does not prescribe a maximum number of
employees. The number of employees is taken into account during the CUP process.

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCACHTER to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

Mrs. Inadomi Halvorsen stated that she has leased to other tenants who have not had to obtain
a CUP in order to get a business license for acupuncture, specifically in the 655 Deep Valley Drive
building. She stated that she was surprised that Ms. Kang (the applicant) would be required to go
through this process.

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR, seconded by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

COMMISSIONER OLSON made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS to,

  Adopt Resolution No. PA-230113, approving the project.

AYES: Yoo, Medawar, Olson, Romanelli, Nicklas, Schachter
NOES:
ABSENT: Friedman
ABSTAIN:

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved a resolution, approving a
Conditional Use Permit (CUP) for a medical office use in an existing office park located at 4040
Palos Verdes Drive North, Suite #101. There is a 20-day appeal period where any member of the
public or the City Council by their own motion may appeal this project.

 7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 230037; LOCATION: CITYWIDE; COMPREHENSIVE
  ZONING CODE UPDATE TO IMPLEMENT THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES GENERAL
  PLAN

Community Development Director Naughton provided a presentation summarizing the staff
report. The discussion will be on the Vision Plan of the Commercial District and its two main
components, which include the Desired Urban Form and Circulation and Connectivity. The focus
for the meeting is on the Desired Urban Form to help develop the district standards.

Street Front and Ground-Floor Setbacks

  •  Proposed: Minimum or zero setbacks
  •  Existing: Average of a minimum of 15 feet and in no case less than 6 feet.

Director Naughton provided the following discussion questions:

  •  Rather than minimum street setbacks, would it be appropriate to establish maximum street
  setbacks?
  •  In the case of larger street setbacks for outdoor dining or similar use, what would be an
  appropriate maximum allowable setback?
  •  Do we want to prescribe corner setbacks to accommodate public or semi-public use?

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR asked if this would apply to new structures, and for example, a façade
remodel of the Promenade Mall. Director Naughton stated that it would apply to both.

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR stated that he is a proponent of outdoor dining and proposed minimum
5 feet and maximum 20 feet with staff to determine the appropriate setback on a case-by-case
basis.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS, Director Naughton stated that objective
criteria is necessary to include in the code since, for example, residential in the Commercial
District will no longer require a CUP and a lot of the discretionary review will need to be built into
the code.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Director Naughton stated that SB9
does not apply in the Commercial District.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER YOO, Director Naughton stated that the desire in
the General Plan is to develop with the pedestrian in mind and avoid fields of surface parking with
development in the back; for smaller sites, there may be a need for structure parking.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked about the corner of 961 Silver Spur Road and asked if
there are any restrictions for people to use the area that is setback from the street. Director
Naughton stated that she will look back to the approving resolution.

COMMISSIONER OLSON proposed a minimum setback of 15 feet and allowing 50% of the
building to encroach up to 5 feet in order to prevent the “block” look and allow for outdoor seating.
He also suggested providing specific setback requirements for each street. In addition, he asked
if developers might be allowed to cantilever the second story out to the 5 foot setback.

Director Naughton stated that at the next meeting there will be a discussion on connectivity.

Massing

  •  Proposed: Varied massing, forms, and materials. Desired scale of three to four stories.
  •  Existing: Maximum building height is 44 feet above grade or three stories, including any
  required parapets.

Director Naughton provided the following discussion questions:

  •  Should the code specify articulation requirements, such as horizontal and vertical
  articulation (plane/façade breaks or stepbacks)?
  •  If appropriate to increase the maximum building height, should a maximum number of
  stories be retained in the code or should it rely on building height alone?

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS, Director Naughton stated that the

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING

  3
 Housing Element projections were based on the density at the time that the Housing Element was
drafted, which was 22 du/acre. Since there was no desire to increase density in the residential
district the focus was on the commercial district and the likelihood that these units could be
accommodated. The density in the Land Use Element was increased due to the market study that
was performed as part of the Land Use Element focused plan, which found that a higher density
would need to be allowed to result in a positive residual land value.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI, Director Naughton stated that the
maximum height will need to be increased and agreed that the three-story limit needs to be
changed.

COMMISSIONER OLSON stated that there should be a height limitation that changes depending
on the density of the development.

Director Naughton explained that the city has a Density Bonus Program.

A brief discussion ensued on the height versus the number of stories.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that he can support the proposed scale of three to four
stories.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS asked if there was an assumption of having taller buildings. Director
Naughton stated that the assumption is looking at dwelling units per acre which could be
accommodated on the opportunity sites.

Director Naughton stated that the challenge is that a CUP is no longer required for residential in
the commercial district and objective design guidelines are required to certify the city’s Housing
Element.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Director Naughton stated that
listing the number of stories will raise challenges as opposed to having maximum building heights
and additional provisions.

Director Naughton stated that staff will provide renderings to get a better idea of what these
buildings will look like.

Smaller Block Patterns

  •  Proposed: Mid-block passages to connect pedestrians through the block and create
  internal addresses for building facing the pedestrian space.
  •  Existing: No provisions for creation of smaller block patterns.

Director Naughton provided the following discussion questions:

  •  How could the code incentivize the creation of smaller block patterns?

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if the objective is to connect Silver Spur and Deep Valley
with walkways and streets, and how to do this without condemning someone’s property. Director
Naughton stated that the objective is to break up the long block patterns and create a
public/private space for people to stop.

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR stated that it may be more feasible to repurpose or redesign the
Promenade Mall and provide these ideas to the new owners.

In response to a question to VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR, Director Naughton stated that in order for
the Housing Element to be certified the city does need to make programmatic changes.

COMMISSIONER OLSON suggested that a discussion be held with the developers to answer
these questions.

Flexible Ground Floor Space

  •  Proposed: Allowing residential or other non-commercial use of space until there is market
  demand for commercial use.
  •  Existing: Currently no requirements that non-residential be on the ground floor.

Director Naughton provided the following discussion questions:

  •  What types of uses should remain conditionally permitted?

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, APRIL 3, 2023
  4
   •  What are the issues related to residential unit loss in the case of flex space converting
  from residential to non-residential?

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR asked if there has always been a provision for a certain number of retail
in mixed-use developments in the commercial district. Director Naughton stated that the number
of non-commercial is not prescribed in the code and it has been a discretionary review.

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR stated that it should be required that there be retail in mixed-use
developments.

COMMISSIONER OLSON asked if it could be required that mixed-use developments have
residential floors be 100% occupied before flex space can be instituted in order to prevent
commercial to be turned into residential.

CHAIR YOO asked if businesses are allowed to operate on rooftops. Director Naughton stated
that there are no provisions in the code for this right now, but it may be something to consider.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS, Director Naughton stated that the
General Plan is the overall vision and the Zoning Code is the implementation; it will not deliver
the vision exactly but will do the best it can to implement what is in the General Plan.

Director Naughton stated that the current list of uses will be emailed to the Planning Commission
for further review at the next meeting.

Style and Variety

  •  Proposed: Locally used materials, such as terra cotta tile roofs and stucco walls, natural
  colors. Stone and brick as accent materials. Overhangs, porches, balconies and other
  shaded space.
  •  Existing: No specific provisions in the code. Specific style and variety criteria are left to
  discretionary review of each individual project.

Director Naughton provided the following discussion questions:

  •  Should the code be flexible to different architectural styles?
  •  How detailed should the code be in listing architectural style and materials?.

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR stated that he prefers not to restrict developers from proposing various
styles.

COMMISSIONER OLSON stated that there should be flexibility for creativity in design.

In a question by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS, Director Naughton suggested adding prohibitions
to the code for materials that should not be allowed in order to encourage high quality materials.

Director Naughton thanked the Planning Commission for their excellent work.

9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR asked about the completion of the repaving on Silver Spur Road.
Director Naughton stated that it should be completed by next week, April 7.

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, FEBRUARY 28, 2023

VICE CHAIR made a motion to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEM NO. 11A

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

12.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR YOO adjourned the meeting at 9:16 p.m.
